title: Tree Removal
description: Safe removal of dead, damaged or dangerous trees across Canberra, including tight spaces and complex rigging. We leave your site clean.
summary: Safe, efficient removal of dead, damaged or dangerous trees – even in tight spaces.
intro: We always prefer to keep trees where we can. When removal is needed, we take trees down safely and efficiently and leave your site spotlessly clean.

content: Our arborists can also advise on the long-term health of your other trees and on any regulations that apply, so you can plan ahead and make sure all the boxes are ticked.

We have decades of experience removing difficult and dangerous trees in confined spaces. We regularly use complex rigging so the area below – garden beds, glasshouses, pools, lawns, powerlines or houses – is left untouched. When a job calls for it, we work with a local crane service to get it done faster.

sections.heading: When to consider removing a tree
content: You may want to consider removing a tree if it is:

list: dead or diseased
storm damaged
in a dangerous or unstable condition
planted in the wrong spot for its current or future size

title: Tree Pruning
description: Expert tree pruning in Canberra to Australian Standard AS 4373, from large specimen trees to fruit trees. Deadwooding, reduction and formative pruning.
summary: Pruning and shaping to Australian Standards, from large specimen trees to fruit trees.
intro: Pruning is one of our specialties, and a service we take pride in delivering to the highest standard.

content: We prune to the Australian Standard for pruning of amenity trees (AS 4373) and all relevant ACT regulations, with a full understanding of tree biology and how different species behave.
Correct pruning reduces a tree's wind resistance, lowering the chance of branch failure.

As a preferred provider for the Australian National Botanic Gardens and The Prime Minister's Lodge, we have pruned some of Canberra's largest trees. We also regularly prune smaller trees – fruit trees for better crops, specimen trees for appearance, and young trees to set good structure.

list.text: Removing dead, diseased or dying branches, down to an agreed size (usually 3 cm).

Removing weak or poorly formed growth while a tree is young (usually 5–15 years old) to build good structure, reduce future weaknesses and help it establish on sites with growth constraints (AS 4373-2007, section 7.2.5).
Selective pruning to restore a tree's natural form after poor past pruning, storm damage, dieback or disease. Usually best done over several visits so the tree can make the most of its new growth.
Selectively thinning the crown by removing lower-order branches, to reduce leaf mass, wind resistance and weight and let air and sunlight through the canopy (AS 4373-2007, section 7.2.3).
Reducing the overall size of the canopy by an agreed amount. It often slows growth so you can keep a tree at its current size for longer, and needs an ongoing pruning programme to maintain.

Removing specific whole branches – for example, branches that pose a risk to people, buildings or structures, or that are too close to powerlines. Some large-branch removals need ACT Government approval; if so, we'll let you know when we quote.
Opening up the tree to let in light and air, encouraging better fruiting.
Removing specific branches that are causing you a problem.

sections.heading: Does your tree need pruning?
content: Your trees may benefit from pruning if they have:

list: excessive end weight (foliage concentrated towards the ends of branches)
structural defects such as inclusions, cavities, rot or disease
low branches that block pedestrian or mower access

content: Pruning can also:

list: let more light into your garden or property
remove dead or diseased branches
clear branches and foliage from powerlines, structures or buildings
shape a specimen tree in your yard
remove or reduce unwanted growth

title: Stump Grinding
description: Stump grinding across Canberra to stop regrowth, remove trip hazards and clear the way for replanting. Our fleet of grinders reaches tight spots.
summary: Fast, cost-effective stump removal that stops regrowth and clears the way for replanting.
intro: Tree stumps can be unsightly, get in the way and create hazards. Stump grinding is the most efficient, cost-effective way to remove them, preventing regrowth and the spread of disease.

content: Our fleet of stump grinders lets us reach even the hardest-to-access stumps.

Our operators use safety barricades to protect nearby houses, windows and gardens, and we complete a Before You Dig Australia (BYDA) check before grinding, so we can safely avoid underground services.

sections.heading: Why remove a stump?
content: Left in the ground, stumps can:

list: become trip hazards
get in the way of replanting
become nesting sites for termites
look untidy in lawns
reshoot into full-sized trees with much weaker structure

title: Powerline Clearance
description: Evoenergy-accredited powerline tree clearance in Canberra. Trained to work near live lines, so most jobs don't need a power outage.
summary: Evoenergy-accredited clearing of trees near powerlines and service lines.
intro: ACT property owners are legally responsible for keeping their trees clear of powerlines and service lines.

content: Trees growing too close to powerlines can cause blackouts, start fires and increase the risk of electrocution.

Our staff are trained and accredited to the highest level to work near live powerlines, so most jobs don't need a power outage. If an outage is needed, we arrange the whole process for you with Evoenergy.

sections.heading: Evoenergy accredited
content: You can rest assured that we are:

list: accredited by Evoenergy to the highest level (high voltage) to work on trees near powerlines
fully trained and qualified in vegetation management
trained and reassessed every year, so our qualifications and methods stay up to date

title: Arborist Consultation & Reports
description: Diploma-qualified consulting arborists in Canberra: tree health checks, risk assessments (QTRA, TRAQ), tree management plans, root damage and disease advice.
summary: Independent advice and written reports from Diploma-qualified consulting arborists.
intro: Our Diploma-qualified consulting arborists give objective, independent advice about your trees – verbally on site, or in a written report.

sections.heading: Health and condition consultation
content: If you're worried about a tree's structure, health, condition or life expectancy, about falling or overhanging limbs – or something just doesn't look right – a detailed inspection with one of our consulting arborists will help put your mind at ease.
We'll identify the key issues and explain them in plain terms. Our goal is objective, impartial advice about your tree.
Consultations are charged, which helps fund ongoing training for our consulting arborists so you get the most up-to-date advice.
If an aerial inspection would help, our climbing consulting arborist can climb and inspect the tree and give you a full report on the findings.

sections.heading: Need something in writing?
content: We can provide brief field notes outlining your trees and situation, or a full, referenced tree report for dealing with third parties such as ACAT, the Tree Protection Unit, planning authorities or body corporate committees.
Our consultants are members of Arboriculture Australia and bound by its Code of Ethics.

sections.heading: Tree risk assessment
content: Worried about your family's or property's safety because of large trees nearby? The risk from trees is often overestimated, and it takes a trained professional to assess it properly.
Our Diploma-level consulting arborists are qualified in both internationally recognised tree risk assessment systems:

list: QTRA (Quantified Tree Risk Assessment)
TRAQ (Tree Risk Assessment Qualification)

content: We can inspect your trees and give you a verified risk assessment, either verbally or as a full report. Assessments can include work that would reduce the risk – but if the assessment doesn't call for any work, we won't recommend it.

sections.heading: Tree management plans for development sites
content: If you're planning to build, excavate or develop near a regulated tree, or near any tree on a neighbouring property, you need to comply with AS 4970 (Protection of trees on development sites).

This starts with a preliminary tree assessment to work out which trees need protection or removal, followed by a Tree Management Plan (TMP) to protect the trees and their root zones during construction, so they're still viable when the project is finished.

We prepare comprehensive reports and TMPs to support your development, but the ACT Government makes the final decision on which works are approved, so compromises are sometimes needed to reach a workable result.

The first step is an on-site consultation with our arborist to understand your needs and plan how to meet them. A TMP is best prepared early, but we also have experience preparing remedial plans when needed.

sections.heading: Tree root damage
content: Tree roots in pipes and root damage to buildings, paths and driveways are common problems. We have a lot of experience helping people deal with them, with clear advice and reports.

If you're not sure what you need, an initial on-site consultation will work it out. From there we can give you clear information on the likelihood of damage, possible outcomes and any recommended work.

sections.heading: Disease identification and treatment
content: Does your tree look different from usual – fewer flowers, holes in the leaves, fungus? Our arborists can come to you to inspect, diagnose and, if needed, treat your trees.

There's a huge range of tree pests and diseases. Some are easy for homeowners to spot; others need expert investigation. Acting early is usually best: it might be drought stress, which is relatively easy to fix if caught in time, or something more complex.
Treatment can be as simple as mulch and water, or may involve spraying or injecting. We'll always explain your options so you can make an informed decision.

Our consulting arborists are qualified to Diploma of Arboriculture level (AQF 5) and experienced in developing pest and disease management programmes. Life as an urban tree is hard, and sometimes they need extra care to thrive.

sections.heading: Elm leaf beetle treatment
content: Elm leaf beetle (Pyrrhalta luteola) has been in the Canberra region for many years. Damage to elms has eased recently, but specimen trees often still need treatment to keep them healthy.
Signs of infestation include:

list: chewed holes in the leaves in October
browning leaves, most obvious from December to April – look closely and you'll see the leaf surface has been chewed off
leaf drop after browning in heavy infestations; badly infested trees often decline over several years and are removed unless the problem is caught and treated early

content: Treatment options:

list.text: Best done in November when the tree is in full leaf, to maximise uptake of the treatment (imidacloprid) and minimise beetle damage.
Done in early September so emerging leaves take up the treatment. This method can affect soil life around the tree.

content: Whichever option you choose, there will still be some chewing damage before the beetles die. Elm leaf beetle is especially damaging because every stage, from larvae to adult beetles, feeds on the leaves – often over several generations a year.

title: Cabling & Bracing
description: Tree cabling and bracing in Canberra to support weak unions and co-dominant stems, so you can keep the trees you love and reduce risk.
summary: Dynamic and steel cabling to support structurally weak trees you want to keep.
intro: Trees add environmental, financial and personal value to homes, workplaces and communities. Cabling and bracing can help you keep a tree you love while reducing the risk of failure.

content: Trees with multiple trunks (co-dominant stems) can be structurally weaker than ideal, and unions like these can fail. Other defective unions or tree parts can also be more likely than average to fail.

We'll inspect your trees, assess any structural weakness, and recommend whether bracing will help you keep them – and which cabling or bracing system suits your situation. The result: you keep the trees you love, with the peace of mind that you've done everything you can to reduce the risk.

sections.heading: Cabling and bracing systems
content: We offer two main types:

list.text: A synthetic cable slung between branches or trunks with a little slack. The tree can still move naturally in the wind, so no shear point is created, but branches can't spread far enough to fail. In the unlikely event of a failure, the cable catches the failed part.
Gives more holding strength than dynamic cabling. Often used where a tree has already failed and needs to be winched back together and held in place.

sections.heading: Why cable or brace a tree?

list.text: reduces the chance of failure in a healthy tree with a structural weakness.
extends the life of a damaged tree.
reduces the risk a tree poses.

title: Commercial Tree Services
metaTitle: Commercial Tree Services & Site Clearance Canberra
description: Commercial tree removal and site clearance in Canberra for builders and civil contractors. Compliance packages, SWMS, clear start dates and reliable equipment.
summary: Site clearance and tree works for builders and civil contractors, with full compliance packages.
intro: Large civil and construction projects need careful planning, compliance and training to run safely and efficiently. Tree removal and site clearance are often among the first jobs on site, so we work as part of your trades team to keep the project moving.

sections.heading: Site inspections
content: Timing matters on commercial jobs. Our consultants can meet you on site, inspect it with your representative, or work from plans to give you an accurate estimate, with options if you need them.
We give clear start dates, from immediately to further ahead. Once scope and quote are agreed, we supply our compliance package to suit your site.

sections.heading: Compliance
content: Safety is the top priority on every site. Our company and personnel compliance packages are prepared in advance and kept up to date, including:

list: Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS) for all high-risk activities
a WHS plan setting out how we manage our workers' health and safety
licences and certifications, including White Card, asbestos awareness, chainsaw and chipper operation, arboriculture qualifications and Evoenergy qualifications

content: We're happy to prepare a compliance package tailored to your site's WHS requirements.

sections.heading: Equipment
content: As one of Canberra's longest-established tree companies, we've invested in the best equipment available. With multiple trucks, chippers, wood loaders and stump grinders, we work efficiently.
Our equipment is serviced regularly, with daily checks and records kept, so we can rely on it – and you can rely on us.

sections.heading: Staff and delivery
content: All our staff hold White Cards and asbestos awareness certification, and have extensive experience on large-scale works. That lets us plan efficient, safe work programmes on site.
Our recent large-scale projects have all finished well within the estimated timeframes, helping lead contractors stay ahead of schedule.

list.text: Large-scale clearance of 120+ large trees for an electrical easement for a new substation and high-voltage transmission lines. We worked closely with the on-site environmental officer to create and install habitat hollows and nest boxes in neighbouring trees.
Clearance of 60 trees and remedial pruning of neighbouring trees for a future health facility, with on-site consultation so excavation complied with the Tree Management Plan.

Clearance of 80 large trees next to existing buildings for the new Research School of Physics and Engineering off Parkes Way, complying with the NCA Tree Management Plan, with ongoing remediation as the plan changed.
